title: Disjointness probability of the hard distribution
statement: Fix a positive integer $n$, and draw a hard sample $\omega$ uniformly at random from the finite sample space of the hard distribution on $n$ coordinates. Then the disjointness event — the event that Alice's input set $X(\omega)$ and Bob's input set $Y(\omega)$ are disjoint — has probability exactly $3/4$.
hypotheses_covered: uniform probability measure on the finite hard-sample space
replaced: The hard distribution generates disjoint inputs with probability $3 / 4$.
